name: CA-38
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting district carries an eight-point Democratic lean and strong Democratic fundamentals
Solis holds a large resource advantage: about $1.5 million raised and outside support, versus no reported fundraising for Casas

model.rationale: The district's eight-point Democratic lean, Solis's decisive fundraising and outside-spending edge, and market pricing near 97 percent for a Democratic win all point the same direction, with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or a wave of Republican spending behind Casas would be the first sign of a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.

overview:
California's 38th District is an open seat created by redistricting, with an eight-point Democratic lean in its partisan baseline, and the fundamentals point clearly toward the Democratic side. Hilda Solis has raised about $1.5 million and holds roughly $285,000 on hand, with outside groups spending in her support and nothing opposing her. Republican Pedro Casas shows no reported fundraising in the available data.

No general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and candidate resources. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. The expected margin is roughly twenty points Democratic, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling. Nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive general election.
